sections.label: Fit
sections.text:
Curator assessment, recorded against the funder's own page on the date shown.[^2] THE HEADLINE OPEN CALL IN THIS CHUNK, and the only one in chunk 1 with a live future deadline MEASURE could realistically meet.[^2] Cycle dates are stated on the funder's own guidelines page WITH EXPLICIT YEARS, so no year inference is involved: opens Tuesday 26 May 2026, closes Wednesday 26 August 2026 at noon (12pm) CST, decisions by 21 September 2026.[^2] As of 2026-08-02 that is 24 days of runway.[^2] IDENTITY CONFLICT INVESTIGATED AND RESOLVED, since this is the one line anyone will act on.[^2] The apparent problem was that EIN 742847652 files with the IRS as ALICE KLEBERG REYNOLDS MEYER FDN TR while the website at akrfoundation.org calls itself THE ALICE KLEBERG REYNOLDS FOUNDATION, with no Meyer.[^2] Four converging checks say they are the same trust and the website simply uses a shortened working name: ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer, used here for the IRS-FILED NAME AND LOCATION it reproduces rather than for any status, shows EIN 74-2847652 as Alice Kleberg Reynolds Meyer Fdn Tr, San Antonio TX, a 501(c)(3) private grantmaking foundation tax-exempt since September 1997, with returns filed for 2023, 2024 and 2025 (the 2025 return filed 13 May 2026, so the entity is currently active); the foundation's own guidelines page describes a 50-county south and central Texas service area, which matches the 50-county description attached to EIN 742847652 in every EIN-keyed listing; both are San Antonio with a 1997 formation; and Instrumentl's profile titled Alice Kleberg Reynolds Foundation resolves to the slug alice-kleberg-reynolds-meyer-fdn-tr, i.e.[^2] the same trust under both names.[^2] BEWARE A GENUINE SIBLING: GuideStar carries a separate ALICE KLEBERG REYNOLDS MEYER FOUNDATION at EIN 74-2020227, a DIFFERENT EIN from this row, and Candid carries a profile under key MEYE011; do not merge those records with this one.[^2] GEOGRAPHY, now much stronger than a guess.[^2] The guidelines page names the service area only as 50 specific counties in south and central Texas and publishes the list as a downloadable map rather than as text, so Travis County is still not confirmed IN THE FUNDER'S OWN WORDS.[^2] However the Ann Richards School for Young Women Leaders, an AUSTIN public school in Travis County, publishes a Reach for the Stars sponsor profile of The Alice Kleberg Reynolds Foundation, which is direct third-party evidence that this funder does in fact grant into Austin and Travis County.[^2] Treat Travis County as very likely in scope, and confirm against the county map before drafting.[^2] Programme fit is plausible rather than tailored: eligible purposes are arts/culture, charitable, education, literacy, medical and scientific, and MEASURE's research and evaluation work would need framing under charitable or medical/scientific, with the maternal health equity line the strongest candidate; there is no explicit research, data or public-safety category.[^2] Scale, from aggregators and therefore background only: about 110 grants totalling roughly $1.76M to $1.8M in 2024, most awards in the $5,000 to $25,000 band and a stated range up to $200,000, total assets about $18.8M.[^2] One residual caution: this row arrived qualified 'prior funder by name match, REVIEW REQUIRED' with 0 grants and 0 recipients in the measured pattern, so the tie to MEASURE specifically is unevidenced and may be a name-join artifact; the OPEN CALL, however, does not depend on that tie.[^2] Contact per aggregators: PO Box 2950, Tax Dept Floor 5, San Antonio TX 78299-2950; Frost Bank reported as trustee (not confirmed on the funder's own pages).[^2] Apply by registering the organisation's TIN at akrfoundation.org.[^2]
